chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who kills his slave deliberately: I would like it if he would emancip a neck, and fast for two consecutive months, and feed sixty poor persons, then repentance would be after that.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately killing a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for deliberately killing a slave, prescribing the freeing of a slave, two months of consecutive fasting, and feeding sixty poor people. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a distinct legal precedent for the death of a slave, differentiating it from the general kaffarah for accidental killing, and emphasizes that these acts constitute the completion of repentance (tawbah) in this context.
